description: The Wood Monkey in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1944 and 2004 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Monkey is the Monkey born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the ninth animal. It combines the Monkey's ingenuity with Wood's qualities. Wood Monkey years between 1924 and 2044 are 1944 and 2004. The Monkey's fixed element is Metal.

sections.heading: The Wood Monkey personality
paragraphs: Metal controls Wood, and the Monkey's fixed element is Metal, which means a Wood year sets this sharp, ingenious animal to work on a growing, open-hearted stem. The common picture is a Monkey whose cleverness is shaped by warmth: inventive, curious and sociable, but also unusually interested in fairness and in projects that help others. Wood Monkeys tend to be lively communicators, quick learners and enthusiastic collaborators. Their ideas often have a practical, constructive bent. Because Metal must keep pruning Wood, though, they can feel a push-and-pull between playful experiment and serious purpose, and readings mention restlessness, impatience with routine and a habit of starting new schemes before old ones are finished.

In the five-element scheme, Wood belongs to the east and to the green energy of early spring, and that seasonal image shapes how it colours an animal sign. A Wood stem tends to soften sharp edges and add warmth, curiosity and a cooperative instinct. Traditional texts associate it with benevolence, growth and the wish to build something that lasts beyond the self. People born under a Wood stem are often portrayed as principled, open-handed and hopeful about others. The caution usually attached to Wood is a habit of spreading energy thinly, saying yes to every request and feeling quietly hurt when generosity is not returned in kind.

sections.heading: Wood Monkey at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

The Wood Monkey is the inventor who also wants everyone to enjoy the workshop. Product design, science communication, educational games, software and collaborative engineering are its natural playgrounds, anywhere ingenuity and teamwork meet. It needs puzzles, a long leash and colleagues who laugh at its jokes. Routine reporting bores it, so pairing with a methodical organiser keeps good ideas from evaporating. In relationships, the Wood Monkey is playful, curious and generous with its time, always proposing a new recipe, route or project. It wants a partner who is lively company and open to experiments. Friction arises from distraction: several home projects started at once can leave half-painted walls and promises waiting.

sections.heading: Wood Monkey years and dates
paragraphs: The table from 1924 to 2044 holds 2 Wood Monkey years: 1944, starting Jan 25 and 2004, starting Jan 22. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1944 anyone born before Jan 25 is a Water Goat, not a Wood Monkey. It takes sixty years for the Wood stem and the Monkey branch to coincide again, which is why the same pairing marks grandparents and grandchildren rather than siblings. Every Wood Monkey year is Yang, matching the Monkey's own polarity.

In the sexagenary calendar this is the Jia-Shen year, the Wood stem Jia with the Monkey's branch Shen. Births just before each new year fall in the Water Goat year (before January 25, 1944) and the Water Goat year (before January 22, 2004), and births in the weeks after each Wood Monkey year ends belong to the Wood Rooster. The new year itself fell on a Tuesday in 1944 and Thursday in 2004.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Monkey
paragraphs: Depth over breadth is the classic lesson for a Wood Monkey. Choosing one skill or project to master each year, rather than sampling ten, turns their versatility into expertise. Their quick wit can sometimes outrun tact, so checking how a joke lands is worthwhile. Wood Monkeys tend to love teaching, inventing and group problem-solving; roles combining all three suit them well. Trusting others' slower pace, instead of jumping in to fix things, builds better teams. Outdoor play and hands-on making settle their busy minds. When they let their ingenuity serve something lasting, Wood Monkeys become admired innovators.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Monkey shares the Monkey's San He trine with the Rat and Dragon (the Water trine), its Liu He bond with the Snake, and its Liu Chong clash with the Tiger. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Monkey years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1944 (from January 25, 1944) and 2004 (from January 22, 2004). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Monkey's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Monkey's fixed element is Metal; in the five-element cycles metal controls Wood. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Monkey?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rat and Dragon (San He) and the Snake (Liu He). The Tiger is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Monkey called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Jia-Shen. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Jia, followed by its earthly branch, here Shen for the Monkey, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Monkey different from other Monkeys?
faq.answer: All Monkeys share ingenuity, humour and curiosity. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
